info.title: Gexis Player API
info.description:
The HTTP API of a Gexis Player: everything its own screen and phone page
do goes through it.

**Where:** `http://<player>.local:8090` on the home network, the player's
name in place of `<player>`. **No login:** the API is open to the home
network, as the player's settings are (ADR-0028, ADR-0022) - every route here,
restart and reset included, can be called by anyone on it.

**Stability.** Each operation carries `x-gexis-stability`: *stable* - what an
integration may rely on - or *internal*, the player's own plumbing, free to
change. A stable route changes only with notice in the release notes, and keeps working for a release after (ADR-0152).

**Live state.** `GET /state` upgrades to a WebSocket that sends the whole
state as JSON whenever it changes (schema `State`); `GET /touchpad` is the
phone touchpad's channel. Commands are plain HTTP requests.

**Errors** answer with a status and `{"error": "<what went wrong>"}`.

The decision records cited (`ADR-xxxx`) are in the project's repository under
`docs/decisions/`.

post.summary: Add a backup file from a phone or computer
post.description: The body is the backup file itself, streamed into the Backups share, checked as setup checks one and added to the Restore list; nothing is restored (ADR-0083 as amended 2026-10-17). A file named differently from a backup is given a backup's name; the same backup already there is not added twice. Errors carry `ok: false` beside `error`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name on the phone or computer; used when it is a valid backup name.

requestBody.description: The backup file, as the raw body (not a form).

400.description: The file did not arrive whole, or it is not a gexis backup, holds more than one, has no settings, cannot be read by this version, is from a newer version, or another arrived under its name at that moment.

409.description: Another backup is being added.

413.description: Larger than any gexis backup (1 GiB).

500.description: The player could not keep the file (its card may be full).

get.summary: Download one backup file
get.description: One backup from the Backups share, sent as a file to save on a phone or computer and use in a new card's setup (ADR-0083 as amended, ADR-0131). The name must be a backup's own name and the file is opened without following a link (Finding 125). Sent as `application/octet-stream`, not gzip, so browsers keep the `.tgz` name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The backup's file name, as the `restore` list gives it.

400.description: Not a backup's name (`not a backup`).

404.description: No such backup on the player any more.

post.summary: Accept or reject the open Bluetooth pairing request
post.description: Answers the Bluetooth pairing request currently published in the state's `pairing` field (ADR-0045). A request is open for 30 seconds; an answer that arrives after it has closed gets 409 and never lands on the next request. Used by the panel's pairing frame and by any client that shows that request.

parameters.name: answer
parameters.description: `accept` to pair, `reject` to refuse.

200.description: The answer was given to the open request.

400.description: The answer is neither `accept` nor `reject`.

409.description: No pairing request is open (it was answered, expired or never existed).

503.description: No pairing agent is wired up in this core.

get.summary: Enrichment for the track playing now
get.description: What is known about what is playing beyond what the renderer said: biography, pictures, lyrics, release facts (ADR-0012, ADR-0040). A route rather than part of /state because it is wanted only while a tab is open and takes seconds. When pending is true a provider had not finished and the client asks again; it compares track with what is playing before drawing. The sweep's portrait is used when there is one (ADR-0075), and a cover is looked for only when the renderer sent none.

200.description: The enrichment, or track null and empty enrichment when nothing is playing.

503.description: Enrichment is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: Read what a hardware report would carry
get.description: What the device reads of its sound card and screen, for the hardware feedback sheet to show before anything is sent (ADR-0126).

get.summary: Download the prepared hardware feedback as text
get.description: The kept feedback as one readable text file, to send by e-mail, made from the link it was prepared as (ADR-0138 decision 3). Named `gexis-hardware-<date>.txt`.

404.description: No feedback is prepared for the hardware in use.

post.summary: Get the hardware issue form's pre-filled link
post.description: The GitHub issue form's address, pre-filled with the facts, the owner's answers, the test tones and the screen check this feedback ran (ADR-0126). Preparing it dismisses the System page's prompt and keeps the feedback, to be sent again (ADR-0126 amended 2026-10-11).

400.description: The body is not an object (`expected an object`).

get.summary: Read the last hardware feedback prepared
get.description: The last feedback prepared - when, the board and screen, and the link to send it again - for the System row (ADR-0126 amended 2026-10-11). Forgotten, and null, once the sound card or screen in use has changed.

post.summary: Forget the kept hardware feedback
post.description: *Start over*: forgets the kept feedback (ADR-0126 amended 2026-10-11). Takes no body.

get.summary: Read the System page's hardware feedback prompt
get.description: The one line offered after a week on a board or screen that is not Tested, or null (ADR-0126 decision 1). Reading it records when each piece of hardware was first seen.

post.summary: Dismiss the hardware feedback prompt
post.description: Dismisses the prompt for good for the hardware in use; another board or screen later is asked about in its own time (ADR-0126 decision 1). Takes no body.

post.summary: Show or take down the screen test pattern
post.description: Puts the test pattern on the panel, asked for from a phone, or takes it down (ADR-0126): the visualiser is lowered and a screen in standby woken first. The pattern goes away by itself after 120 s. Taking it down answers `{"ok": true}`.

200.description: Shown (the check's number and touch), or taken down (`ok`).

post.summary: Send the panel's four corner taps
post.description: The panel's four corner taps, in the screen's own pixels, measured here against 6 % of the diagonal and shown on the phone (ADR-0126 decision 2). The pattern is taken down.

400.description: The body is not valid (`bad taps`).

409.description: No test pattern is being shown, or `seq` is not the one showing.

post.summary: Play the test tones through the player's output
post.description: A tone at 44.1, 96 and 192 kHz through the player's own output, and the rate the card ran at for each (ADR-0126). Only when nothing is playing: a test never cuts into music. One set at a time. Takes no body.

409.description: The tones are already playing, there is no output, something is playing or a paused source holds the card, or a source took the card while they played.

get.summary: Check whether the configured idle page can be shown
get.description: Probes the web page set in the `idle_url` setting, asked each time the idle screen opens because reachability changes while the device runs (ADR-0019). The panel embeds the page in a frame, which cannot tell it why it is blank, so the core checks: unconfigured, unreachable within 5 seconds, an HTTP error status, or headers that forbid framing (X-Frame-Options, or a CSP frame-ancestors without `*`) all make it not embeddable, and the panel shows its own idle screen instead. Headers only: a page that refuses framing from script still passes.

200.description: Whether the page can be embedded, and why not.

503.description: The idle page probe is not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Get the next background picture for the idle or home screen
get.description: One route for every background source: the background setting (`idle_background`, or `waiting_background` with `for=home`) decides whether the answer is one of the player's own pictures (ADR-0133), an artist picture from the library, a downloaded Pixabay picture, a picture put on the device, or none (Black). With `w` and `h`, each picture is also placed for that screen by what it shows (ADR-0120): `place` gives its vertical position and width, and a picture too big for the screen is passed over for the next, up to four times. A picture never repeats the one already on screen when there is another (ADR-0047 §2e). When the picture changes is the panel's to count; nothing in the core holds a timer. A source that cannot answer is a 200 with a reason in `error`.

parameters.name: for
parameters.description: `home` reads the home (waiting) screen's background rows; anything else, or none, reads the idle screen's.

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: The asking screen's width in pixels. Placement happens only when both `w` and `h` are integers from 100 to 8000.

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: The asking screen's height in pixels; see `w`.

200.description: The next picture, `off` for a black background, or a reason in `error`.

503.description: Settings are not wired up in this core, or the background is `Wallpapers online` or `Wallpapers on device` and the wallpaper source is not wired up.

get.summary: Get a picture somebody put on this device
get.description: Serves one picture from the device's own wallpaper folder, as named in a `/idle/wallpaper` answer. The name may contain folders; it is resolved and must stay inside the wallpaper folder and end in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp, so a path that climbs out of it is refused - the route is reachable from the LAN (ADR-0028).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The picture's name relative to the device's wallpaper folder, URL-encoded; may contain slashes (sub-folders).

404.description: No such picture: wrong suffix, outside the folder, or not a file.

503.description: The wallpaper source is not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Get one of the player's own wallpapers
get.description: Serves one of the pictures that ship with the player (ADR-0133). Only a name listed in the pictures' credits file is served, so nothing else on the disk is reachable. Sent with `Cache-Control: max-age=86400`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The picture's name as the credits list holds it, including its set folder; contains a slash (for example `dusk/example.webp`).

200.description: The picture file. The pictures shipped today are WebP; the route itself does not restrict the type.

404.description: The name is not in the credits list, or its file is missing: `no such picture`.

get.summary: Get a downloaded online wallpaper
get.description: Serves one picture downloaded from Pixabay into the wallpaper cache, as named in a `/idle/wallpaper` answer. A file name only, never a path, and only a .jpg: the route is reachable from the LAN (ADR-0028) and a name that could climb out of its directory would serve the disk.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The cached file's name, a single path segment ending in `.jpg`.

404.description: The name is a path, does not end in `.jpg`, or is not in the cache: `no such picture`.

503.description: The wallpaper source is not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Get the forecast the idle screen draws
get.description: The current conditions and the daily forecast for the `weather_location` setting, from Open-Meteo (ADR-0047 §2). Asked by the panel rather than pushed; the core keeps a forecast for fifteen minutes, so a redraw costs nothing and a setting change is picked up on the next ask. The `idle_forecast` setting chooses one day (`Today only`) or three (`3 days`). A refusal is a 200 with a reason in `error`, not an error status: weather switched off, no location set, a place that could not be found, or the forecast unavailable.

200.description: The forecast, or a reason in `error` why there is none.

value.error: That place could not be found.

503.description: Settings or the weather service are not wired up in this core.

post.summary: Play, queue or add a library item to a playlist
post.description: The one route for what a client does to the library (ADR-0038 §5): play an album, artist, track or playlist (in order, or shuffled), append it to the queue, or add its tracks to a library playlist; with kind `queue`, jump to, remove or clear queue positions. Lyrion powers the player on itself when loading (ADR-0038 §4). A 200 means the command was sent; what happened is read from /state (ADR-0037 §1).

400.description: The body is not JSON, or kind/id is missing, or id or playlist_id is not an integer.

404.description: Unknown kind or action; the item does not exist (Lyrion acted on no tracks); action playlist without playlist_id, or playlist_id is not a library playlist.

409.description: The Lyrion player has not been resolved yet, so there is nothing to play on.

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error ("Lyrion unreachable: ...").

503.description: The library is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: What the artist page shows below the discography
get.description: Biography, picture, similar artists and the popular recordings this library holds, for the artist page (ADR-0038 §2). Lyrion's own plugin answers first from the id, then the key-free providers (Wikipedia, ListenBrainz, popular, fanart) fill what it leaves, keyed on the name (ADR-0040 §1). The picture is the artwork sweep's when it has one, then fanart's, then Lyrion's (ADR-0075). Without an id, Lyrion's plugin is not asked and popular is empty.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The artist's name.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Lyrion's album-artist id.

400.description: id is not an integer, or name is missing or blank.

503.description: Enrichment is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: Photos for a batch of artists
get.description: A photo URL per artist id, for the artists a screen is about to draw rather than the whole library (Finding 035). The artwork sweep's fanart portrait answers first and Lyrion's artist-information plugin only for the rest (ADR-0068, ADR-0059; ADR-0040 §1). An artist with neither is null.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated Lyrion artist ids; only the first 80 are read. None answers {}.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Square size in pixels: 200 (thumbnail) or 600 (large).

400.description: An id or size is not an integer, or size is not 200 or 600.

503.description: Artist info is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: Read a library list
get.description: Reads only, for the designed screens: the core runs typed Lyrion queries and returns the fields the screens draw; the client never sends a Lyrion command (ADR-0038 §5). Lists are cached until Lyrion's lastscan changes. `counts` is the root's cards, `strip` the home strip in the shape the home_strip setting names, `new` the newest albums (ten), `artists` a page of album artists, `playlists` the library playlists (never a plugin's).

parameters.name: what
parameters.description: Which list.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: First row, for a paged read (artists, a playlist's tracks). Negative is read as 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows wanted, clamped to 1-1000. For `strip` it is the length only when the home_strip_count setting is unset (clamped 4-20).

200.description: The list; its shape depends on `what`.

400.description: offset, limit or the id is not an integer.

404.description: No such read (an unlisted combination of what/id/sub), or the album or playlist does not exist - a rescan renumbers every id (Finding 029 §4).

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error ("Lyrion unreachable: ...").

503.description: The library is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: Read one album or playlist
get.description: Reads only, for the designed screens: the core runs typed Lyrion queries and returns the fields the screens draw; the client never sends a Lyrion command (ADR-0038 §5). Lists are cached until Lyrion's lastscan changes. `albums/{id}` is an album with its tracks in track order; `playlists/{id}` a page of a library playlist's tracks (offset/limit). An artist has no read of its own: use its sub-reads.

parameters.name: what
parameters.description: Kind of item.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Lyrion's id for the item.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: First row, for a paged read (artists, a playlist's tracks). Negative is read as 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows wanted, clamped to 1-1000. For `strip` it is the length only when the home_strip_count setting is unset (clamped 4-20).

200.description: The album, or the playlist page.

400.description: offset, limit or the id is not an integer.

404.description: No such read (an unlisted combination of what/id/sub), or the album or playlist does not exist - a rescan renumbers every id (Finding 029 §4).

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error ("Lyrion unreachable: ...").

503.description: The library is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: Read an artist's albums or genres
get.description: Reads only, for the designed screens: the core runs typed Lyrion queries and returns the fields the screens draw; the client never sends a Lyrion command (ADR-0038 §5). Lists are cached until Lyrion's lastscan changes. `artists/{id}/albums` is the artist's discography, newest first (undated last, same year by title), each with Lyrion's release_type; `artists/{id}/genres` their genre names, without Lyrion's "No Genre". An unknown artist id answers an empty list, not 404.

parameters.name: what
parameters.description: Only artists has sub-reads.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Lyrion's album-artist id.

parameters.name: sub
parameters.description: Which sub-read.

400.description: The id is not an integer.

404.description: No such read (an unlisted combination of what/id/sub).

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error ("Lyrion unreachable: ...").

503.description: The library is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: Home-screen tiles for Lyrion's own menus
get.description: The tiles Extended navigation adds to the home screen: My Music, Favourites, Apps and any top category an app adds (ADR-0118 A). While it is off (or the menus are not wired up) the answer is on false and no tiles, so a client asks once and knows. Always 200; Lyrion being unreachable is reported in error.

post.summary: Play, add or play next a Lyrion menu item
post.description: Runs what Lyrion itself offers for an item this core issued - play, add to the end, or play next (Lyrion's add-hold) - and nothing else (ADR-0118 D). The item's can list says which apply.

400.description: The body is not JSON or has no handle.

404.description: Unknown action; unknown handle; the item cannot do that action; or the Lyrion player has not been resolved yet.

409.description: Extended navigation is off (settings lms_extended_nav off, or lms_enabled false).

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error ("Lyrion unreachable: ...").

503.description: The menus is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: One page of a Lyrion menu list, by handle
get.description: One page of the list a handle names, as rows with handles of their own. The client never sends a Lyrion command; the core acts only on handles it issued, and leaves out the player's settings, entries that write, presets and one-off actions (ADR-0118 C, D, J). Handles are opaque, bounded in number and not kept across restarts.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: A handle from /menus, a previous page or a search.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: First entry.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Entries wanted; at most 100 for a folder.

400.description: start or count is not a number.

404.description: Unknown handle, or the handle is not a list.

409.description: Extended navigation is off (settings lms_extended_nav off, or lms_enabled false).

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error ("Lyrion unreachable: ...").

503.description: The menus is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: Where each letter starts in a Lyrion menu list
get.description: The jump rail's index for a list: the library's lists are read whole once and the first position of each letter kept (for half an hour); a service's list, or one without letters, answers empty (ADR-0118).

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: A list's handle.

404.description: Unknown handle.

409.description: Extended navigation is off (settings lms_extended_nav off, or lms_enabled false).

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error ("Lyrion unreachable: ...").

503.description: The menus is not wired up (the core started without it).

post.summary: Answer a Lyrion menu search item
post.description: Answers a search item (kind search) with typed text and returns its first page of results, with a handle for the results list (ADR-0118 E).

requestBody.description: The search item's handle and the text.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or handle or text is missing.

404.description: Unknown handle, the handle is not a search, or the text is empty.

409.description: Extended navigation is off (settings lms_extended_nav off, or lms_enabled false).

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error ("Lyrion unreachable: ...").

503.description: The menus is not wired up (the core started without it).

get.summary: Read the cable's address settings
get.description: The port's IPv4 address as NetworkManager has it - method, address, gateway, DNS - with the row's summary line and, while a change waits for Keep, the pending address (ADR-0123).

503.description: Neither the cable's nor the Wi-Fi's address handling is wired up in this core (`not wired up`).

post.summary: Change the cable's address, pending Keep
post.description: Applies an address - Automatic, or Manual with gateway and DNS - and starts a 60 s wait: it is kept only once confirmed with `POST /network/keep` from the new address, or put back as it was (ADR-0123). The address to open is in the answer. Only one change, cable or Wi-Fi, may wait at a time.

400.description: The body is not an object, the address, gateway or DNS is not valid (a sentence for the phone), the method is neither, the port has no connection, a change is under way or waiting on this port, or NetworkManager refused it (nothing was changed).

409.description: A change on the other port is waiting to be kept or being applied.

503.description: Neither the cable's nor the Wi-Fi's address handling is wired up in this core (`not wired up`).

post.summary: Keep the address change that is waiting
post.description: Keep for whichever port's change is waiting (ADR-0123). Accepted only when the request arrives at the new address, which proves it works, or from the panel on loopback; otherwise the old address comes back when the wait runs out. Takes no body.

409.description: Nothing is waiting to be kept, or the request did not arrive at the new address (the error names the address to open).

503.description: Neither the cable's nor the Wi-Fi's address handling is wired up in this core (`not wired up`).

get.summary: Read the connected Wi-Fi network's details
get.description: The connected Wi-Fi network's name, signal, speed, band, channel and address, read without a rescan so an open sheet can ask every few seconds (ADR-0123). Answers `{"connected": false}` when there is no connection or NetworkManager is not available.

get.summary: Read the Wi-Fi's address settings
get.description: The port's IPv4 address as NetworkManager has it - method, address, gateway, DNS - with the row's summary line and, while a change waits for Keep, the pending address (ADR-0123). The same handler as `/network/cable`, for the Wi-Fi port.

503.description: Neither the cable's nor the Wi-Fi's address handling is wired up in this core (`not wired up`).

post.summary: Change the Wi-Fi's address, pending Keep
post.description: Applies an address - Automatic, or Manual with gateway and DNS - and starts a 60 s wait: it is kept only once confirmed with `POST /network/keep` from the new address, or put back as it was (ADR-0123). The address to open is in the answer. Only one change, cable or Wi-Fi, may wait at a time. The same handler as `POST /network/cable`, for the Wi-Fi port.

400.description: The body is not an object, the address, gateway or DNS is not valid (a sentence for the phone), the method is neither, the port has no connection, a change is under way or waiting on this port, or NetworkManager refused it (nothing was changed).

409.description: A change on the other port is waiting to be kept or being applied.

503.description: Neither the cable's nor the Wi-Fi's address handling is wired up in this core (`not wired up`).

get.summary: Read the Legal, Credits or Change logs page
get.description: The documents behind Settings' `document` rows: Legal and Credits, built from the list of third-party components the player ships (ADR-0099), and the release notes of the last releases (ADR-0116).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The document.

404.description: No document has that name (`no such document`).

post.summary: Send the panel to a screen
post.description: Asks the panel to go to Home, Now Playing, Lyrics, the track's page, or to minimise, as the phone's sheet does (ADR-0101 as amended 2026-10-05). It counts as attention first, as a touch on the panel does, which also takes the visualiser down; the request then reaches the panel through the live state. Every destination but `home` leads through Now Playing, which exists only while a source is active, so those are refused when nothing is.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Where to send the panel.

200.description: The request was passed to the panel.

404.description: `to` is not one of the destinations: `unknown view <to>`.

409.description: A destination other than `home` was asked for while no source is active: `nothing is playing`.

post.summary: Show or hide the panel's idle screen
post.description: The phone's idle-screen toggle (ADR-0101). It counts as attention first, as a touch on the panel does, so the idle and visualiser timers restart and the visualiser is taken down; the request then reaches the panel through the live state. The answer means the request was passed on; whether the panel shows it arrives in the live state once the panel reports it.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `show` to put the idle screen up, `hide` to take it down.

200.description: The request was passed to the panel.

404.description: `action` is neither `show` nor `hide`: `unknown action <action>`.

post.summary: Report the panel's first painted frame
post.description: The panel reports that it has drawn its first frame, which ends the boot animation (ADR-0043 §3). It is deliberately not tied to the kiosk service going active, which happens a second or two before anything is drawn. Always answers 200, whether or not there was a splash to drop; the core's own on-painted hook runs only for a request from loopback. No body is read.

200.description: Recorded; says whether a boot splash was dropped.

post.summary: Report what the panel is showing
post.description: The panel reports whether its idle screen, its lyrics and its Now Playing screen are up, so the phone's toggles say what the panel shows whatever changed it (ADR-0101, as amended). The values are published in the live state. Accepted from loopback only: a phone saying so would set the toggles to a lie. At least one of the three keys must be present; each value is taken as a boolean.

200.description: The keys that were given, each as a boolean.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or holds none of `idle`, `lyrics` or `now`.

403.description: The request did not come from the panel (not loopback): `only the panel reports what it shows`.

post.summary: Turn the screen off or on (display standby)
post.description: Puts the panel's screen into standby or brings it out, from a phone or the Settings action (ADR-0135). `on` means standby on, which is the screen off; `off` wakes it. The answer carries whether the screen is in standby once the change has been made.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `on` turns the screen off (standby on); `off` turns it back on.

200.description: Done; whether the screen is now in standby.

404.description: `action` is neither `on` nor `off`: `unknown action <action>`.

503.description: Display standby is not wired up in this core.

post.summary: Show or hide the visualiser
post.description: Raises or lowers the visualiser (the Peppy meters window) over the panel. When asked to show and there is no window while levels are available, the visualiser service is restarted once and the request waits up to 25 seconds for its window; a second request during that restart waits on the same one rather than restarting it again. The answer can therefore take tens of seconds.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `show` raises the visualiser; `hide` lowers it.

200.description: The window was raised or lowered.

404.description: `action` is neither `show` nor `hide`: `unknown action <action>`.

409.description: There was no visualiser window to act on, including after a restart that did not bring one up: `no Peppy screen window to act on`.

503.description: The visualiser is not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Whether part 2 of first use is owed, and its plugins
get.description: What the part 2 page (make it yours, ADR-0149) needs beyond /settings: whether part 2 is owed, done or put off, whether this is a new player's first time (the page then starts from part 2's own defaults rather than the current settings), and the plugins it can switch on.

post.summary: Write part 2's answers and start what they install
post.description: Writes part 2's answers in one go (ADR-0149), each through Settings as if set there; one that refuses is named in failed and the rest go on. Plugins switched on and the visualiser's skins are then followed as downloads on the settling screen (ADR-0128), except what is already installed. Part 2 is marked done. If lms_server was written, the core restarts once those downloads are in, so the new server is used. The settings keys accepted are only part 2's (personalise.checked): lms_enabled, lms_server, lms_extended_nav, lms_library, spotify_enabled, bt_enabled, phone_touchpad, visualiser_skins, viz_timeout, skin_corpus, skin_motion, record_speed, waiting_clock, waiting_background, waiting_wallpaper_styles, idle_enabled, idle_background, wallpaper_styles, idle_clock, idle_weather, weather_location, standby_schedule, standby_times, lyrion-server.music_folder, lyrion-server.usb, lyrion-server.enabled, plexamp.enabled; any other key refuses the whole request.

200.description: Written; what is being waited for.

400.description: The body is not JSON or not an object, settings is not an object, or it holds a key that is not part 2's to set ("not part 2's to set: ...").

503.description: Settings are not wired up in this core.

post.summary: Put part 2 of first use off
post.description: Do it later on part 2 (ADR-0149): marks it put off. On a new player this also switches the Lyrion client off (lms_enabled false), so the player plays what needs nothing set up; asked again from Settings, nothing is changed. Part 2 can be opened again from Settings.

get.summary: This player's name and what it is playing
get.description: What this player says of itself to other players and phones: its name, its `.local` host, a per-process instance id, whether it is playing and through which renderer (ADR-0136). Other Gexis players call this route when they build their list for the phone's player switcher.

get.summary: This player and the other players on the network
get.description: This player's status and those of the other Gexis players found on the network, for the phone's switcher (ADR-0136). The others are found by browsing `_gexis._tcp` over mDNS and asking each one's `/player/status`; the list is kept warm in the background and refreshed every 30 seconds, so the answer is normally immediate. A player that is off, unreachable, too old to announce itself, or that is this player under another mDNS name, is left out.

200.description: This player and the others found.

post.summary: Upload and install a plugin package
post.description: The plugin package (a tar archive with its manifest) as the raw request body, read with its own 200 MB cap (ADR-0106). It is checked before anything is written, installed beside the version before it, and run by a unit the player writes; a first install arrives switched off. The core restarts about 1.5 s after answering.

requestBody.description: The package, as the raw body (not a form).

400.description: The package was refused (`Not installed: <reason>.`).

503.description: Uploads are not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Get a source's glyph
get.description: A plugin's `mark.png`, by its id (ADR-0086); the id is looked up among the plugins loaded at start, never joined onto a path. Cached for a day: the URL the panel is given carries the file's hash as `?v=`, which is not read here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The plugin's id.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: The mark's hash, for caching; ignored.

404.description: No plugin with that id, or it has no mark (`no mark for that source`).

post.summary: Uninstall an uploaded plugin
post.description: Removes an uploaded plugin - its unit switched off, its files, data and settings deleted - or forgets one a restore brought back without its package (ADR-0106). Shipped plugins cannot be uninstalled. The core restarts shortly after answering. Takes no body.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The plugin's id.

404.description: Not an uploaded plugin.

503.description: Uploads are not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Browse one level of Lyrion's radio tree
get.description: One level of Lyrion's radio tree, browsed by handle, never by command (ADR-0038 §5, ADR-0030). No handle is the root. Podcasts and items that ask for typed text (such as a search) are left out. Handles are opaque, bounded in number and not kept across restarts.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: A folder's handle; omitted for the root.

404.description: Unknown handle, or the handle is not a folder.

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error.

503.description: Radio is not wired up (the core started without it).

post.summary: Play or queue a radio station
post.description: Plays a station, or adds it to the queue; only a handle this core issued for a station does anything (ADR-0038 §5). Where the station carries its own stream URL that is played directly.

requestBody.description: The station's handle and the action.

400.description: The body is not JSON or has no handle.

404.description: Unknown action; unknown handle; the handle is not a station; or the Lyrion player has not been resolved yet.

502.description: Lyrion could not be reached or answered with an error.

503.description: Radio is not wired up (the core started without it).

post.summary: Make a renderer take the device
post.description: Asks a renderer to take the device, which is how the panel and phone switch to a source such as Lyrion (ADR-0028's command surface). The renderer must be known and must declare an `activate` control in its capabilities (ADR-0020); one that cannot be activated is refused rather than silently ignored. A renderer that is switched off is not woken first and answers 502 (ADR-0077). A 200 means the renderer's own API accepted the request; the takeover itself arrives on /state.

parameters.name: renderer_id
parameters.description: A renderer id as published under `capabilities` in the state: `lms`, `spotify`, `bluetooth`, or a plugin's id.

404.description: No renderer with that id is in the published capabilities.

409.description: The renderer does not declare an `activate` control.

502.description: The renderer's own API refused or could not be reached, the renderer is switched off, or it declares `activate` without implementing it.

503.description: Activation is not wired up in this core.

post.summary: Pause Lyrion as the device goes down
post.description: Called by the shutdown (gexis-park.service) so that nothing resumes by itself after a restart: the Lyrion player is paused, keeping its queue and position. With `?stop=all`, used before an update installs (ADR-0110 §4), whoever is playing is stopped first. Loopback only.

parameters.name: stop
parameters.description: `all` also stops whichever renderer is playing before Lyrion is paused (an update's shutdown). Any other value is ignored.

200.description: Whether Lyrion was paused. `parked` is false when parking is not wired up or Lyrion could not be paused.

403.description: The request did not come from loopback.

post.summary: Build and download a problem report in one request
post.description: Builds the problem report - the logs, versions, hardware and settings with personal details taken out - and answers it as a zip (ADR-0125). The body may carry the user's own line. Takes about half a minute on a Pi 4; one report at a time. The page uses `/report/prepare` instead (ADR-0138).

409.description: A report is already being prepared.

503.description: The settings store is not wired up in this core (`settings are not wired up`).

get.summary: Download the prepared problem report
get.description: The zip `/report/prepare` made, while it is kept (an hour) (ADR-0138).

404.description: No report is ready.

get.summary: Get a pre-filled GitHub issue link for the report
get.description: The problem's GitHub issue form, filled in with what happened, how often, the version, what was taken out and the log's last errors, kept under GitHub's length (ADR-0138 §3). The file is attached by hand.

404.description: No report is ready.

post.summary: Start preparing a problem report in the background
post.description: Starts the problem report in the background; its checklist is ticked as it goes and read from `/report/status` (ADR-0138 §1). The file and the issue link follow once it is ready. A body that is not an object is treated as empty.

409.description: A report is already being prepared.

503.description: The settings store is not wired up in this core (`settings are not wired up`).

get.summary: Read how far the problem report has got
get.description: The state of the report being prepared and its checklist (ADR-0138 §1); once ready, the file's name, size, contents and what was taken out. A ready report is dropped after an hour.

post.summary: Answer the question that a different screen is attached
post.description: Answers the question asked when a screen other than the kept one is attached (ADR-0109, amended 2026-10-03). Unlike Keep it may come from the panel or a phone, since choosing does not prove that the picture and the touch work, and Keep is still asked on the panel after the restart. `use` switches to the recognised screen (the usual restart and Keep follow), `later` stops asking about that screen, and `choose` lets the panel open the screen list (asked again at the next start if nothing is chosen).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The answer: `use`, `later` (not now) or `choose`.

200.description: `{"ok": true}` when the answer was taken. When no such question is open the status is still 200, with `{"error": "nothing is being asked"}`.

404.description: `action` is not one of the answers, or the answer is not wired up in this core: `unknown answer <action>`.

post.summary: Answer the Keep question after a screen change
post.description: Answers the question shown after the player switched to a new screen: keep it, or go back to the previous one (ADR-0109 decision 2). Keep is pressed on the panel only, since a touch there proves both the picture and the touch input; a phone may answer only when the question says so (`phone` in the live state's `screen_confirm`): a screen without touch such as a TV (ADR-0147 D3), or a listed panel whose touch the player does not recognise (Finding 125). `shown` is the panel reporting that it has drawn the question, which starts the countdown; only the panel may send it.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `keep` keeps the new screen; `revert` goes back to the previous one; `shown` reports that the question is on the glass (panel only).

200.description: The answer was taken. `keep` answers `{"kept": true}`, `revert` answers `{"going_back": true}` (the switch back happens after the answer), `shown` answers `{"shown": true}`.

403.description: Not from the panel (not loopback), and either the action is `shown` (`only the panel reports this`) or the open question does not allow a phone to answer (`only the panel answers this`).

404.description: `action` is not one of the answers, or screen confirmation is not wired up in this core: `unknown answer <action>`.

get.summary: List every setting, grouped as the Settings screen shows them
get.description: Answers every row of the settings registry (ADR-0035), including the ones the screen will not draw: each row carries `visible` and the panel only obeys it (ADR-0044 §6). Lists that are one cheap local read - paired Bluetooth devices, backups (ADR-0083), shares and USB folders (ADR-0115) - arrive with their items; the others carry `discover: true` and are fetched from `/settings/{key}/items`. The header's name, hostname and address come with it (ADR-0048 §5). Fetched again whenever the live state's settings revision moves.

503.description: The settings store is not wired up in this core (`settings are not wired up`).

put.description: Validates the value against the row (ADR-0035), stores it and runs whatever applies it. The answer carries the value as stored and the settings revision the save made. A row marked `restart` restarts the device after answering when its value changed, or only the core when it is marked `"core"` (the Lyrion server). Refusals come back as `{"error": sentence}` with 400 (the value is wrong), 404 (no such key), 405 (the row takes no value), or 409 (not wired, or the option is unavailable on this hardware, ADR-0055).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A setting's key as `/settings` lists it, e.g. `output_mode`, or a plugin's prefixed key such as `beszel.enabled`.

400.description: The body is not `{"value": ...}`, or the value is not valid for the row (the error says why, e.g. `expected true or false`, `expected 0 to 100`, `not an option: ...`).

404.description: No setting has that key (`unknown setting <key>`).

405.description: The row takes no value: an action, readonly, document or non-server list row.

409.description: The row is not wired yet, or the chosen option is locked by the hardware (the reason from the row's `unavailable`).

503.description: The settings store is not wired up in this core (`settings are not wired up`).

post.summary: Run an action row
post.description: Runs an `action` row - a backup, a restart, a factory reset and the like - and answers at once; the action may outlast the request. `POST /settings/backup?before=update` is the updater's own backup: named as such, the oldest of those beyond three deleted, never one taken by hand (ADR-0083). Refusals come back as for PUT.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A setting's key as `/settings` lists it, e.g. `output_mode`, or a plugin's prefixed key such as `beszel.enabled`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only with key `backup`: `update` marks the backup as the updater's own, kept three deep.

404.description: No setting has that key.

405.description: The row is not an action.

409.description: The action is not wired yet.

503.description: The settings store is not wired up in this core (`settings are not wired up`).

get.summary: List the items of a list row
get.description: What a list row's sheet shows (ADR-0044 §1): a Wi-Fi scan, paired Bluetooth devices, the Lyrion servers found (this player's own first), the backups in the share - read every time (ADR-0083) - the music shares' servers announcing themselves (ADR-0115, kept a minute) or the USB drives and folders. A Wi-Fi list without NetworkManager answers no items and an `error`.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A `list` row's key: `wifi`, `bt_trusted`, `lms_server`, `restore`, `lyrion-server.shares` or `lyrion-server.usb_folders`. Another list row answers `{"items": []}`.

parameters.name: saved
parameters.description: `lyrion-server.shares` only: `1` lists the shares added, without searching for servers.

parameters.name: fresh
parameters.description: `lyrion-server.shares` only: `1` searches again instead of reusing the last minute's servers.

404.description: No setting has that key.

405.description: The row is not a list (`<key> is not a list`).

503.description: The settings store is not wired up in this core (`settings are not wired up`).

post.summary: Act on one item of a list row
post.description: Joins or forgets a Wi-Fi network, forgets a Bluetooth device, restores or forgets a backup (ADR-0083: a restore reboots the device after answering), and browses, adds or forgets music shares and USB folders (ADR-0115). A refusal the sheet can show - a wrong password, a server that did not answer - is a 200 with `ok: false` and the sentence; a Wi-Fi join while a cable is plugged in adds a `notice` that the cable stays in use (ADR-0123).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A `list` row's key: `wifi`, `bt_trusted`, `lms_server`, `restore`, `lyrion-server.shares` or `lyrion-server.usb_folders`. Another list row answers `{"items": []}`.

200.description: Done, or refused with a sentence in `error`.

400.description: The body is not `{"name": ..., "action": ...}`, or the action is not one this list takes (`unknown action <action>`).

404.description: No setting has that key.

405.description: The row is not a list, or the list has no per-item action (`lms_server`).

503.description: The settings store is not wired up, or a Wi-Fi action without NetworkManager (`NetworkManager is not available`).

post.summary: Acknowledge a settling screen with a failed download
post.description: The owner's OK on a settling screen that names a download that did not finish (ADR-0128). Ends the settling record and clears it from the live state.

503.description: Settling is not wired up in this core ("not wired up").

post.summary: Put the settling screen away while downloads go on
post.description: The owner put the settling screen away while the downloads go on (ADR-0128 as amended 2026-10-10). The live state is updated at once.

503.description: Settling is not wired up in this core ("not wired up").

get.summary: The answers saved so far in setup, to resume from
get.description: Part 1 of first use (ADR-0149) saves each step in the core as it is completed, so a page that reopens resumes from here (ADR-0104 §4). The Wi-Fi password is never returned, only has_password. Loading this also tells the panel that a phone reached the page (page_opened). Answers only while setup is running.

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up in this core (no setup network manager or setup flow). The error is the phone's generic sentence (setup_flow.said).

post.summary: Save one or more setup answers
post.description: Merges the given answers into those saved and answers all of them, as GET does (ADR-0104 §4). Every key is optional; an unknown key or a value of the wrong type refuses the whole request. A screen and headless are one choice (ADR-0109): a screen sets headless false, headless true drops the screen and the visualiser answer. Changing ssid or password clears the last join's error. Answers only while setup is running.

200.description: All saved answers after the change.

400.description: The body is not JSON or not an object, a key is unknown, a value has the wrong type or is not one of its allowed values, the screen is not a known model, or a screen and headless true were both sent. The error is a sentence for the phone (setup_flow.said).

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up in this core (no setup network manager or setup flow). The error is the phone's generic sentence (setup_flow.said).

post.summary: Upload a backup to restore from in setup
post.description: A backup uploaded from the phone in setup (ADR-0131). The request body is the backup file itself (not a form), streamed to disk under a 1 GiB cap, then checked; a file that is refused is deleted and a backup kept before it stays. On success the backup's review is saved in the answers as backup, start becomes restore, and all the answers are returned. Answers only while setup is running.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's own name, used only for the review: a gexis backup name carries when it was made. Kept as backup.file (first 120 characters).

200.description: All saved answers, with backup holding the review.

400.description: The file did not arrive whole, or it is not a gexis backup that can be restored (backups.Refused, its sentence for the phone).

413.description: The file is larger than any gexis backup (over 1 GiB).

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up in this core (no setup network manager or setup flow). The error is the phone's generic sentence (setup_flow.said).

requestBody.description: The backup file (.tgz) as the raw request body.

delete.summary: Forget the backup uploaded in setup
delete.description: Deletes the backup uploaded in setup and removes backup from the saved answers (ADR-0131). start is left as it was. Answers only while setup is running.

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up in this core (no setup network manager or setup flow). The error is the phone's generic sentence (setup_flow.said).

post.summary: Start applying the setup answers
post.description: Starts applying setup's answers and answers at once with 202 (ADR-0104 §4): the settings first, then the Wi-Fi country from the time zone, then the network join, which loses the phone's page. With start restore, the uploaded backup is put back with what was changed in setup over it, then the player restarts (ADR-0131). A new player is then owed part 2 of first use (ADR-0149). A second call while applying answers keep_question false and starts nothing.

400.description: No network was chosen and the device is not online by cable ("Choose a Wi-Fi network first, or connect the player by cable."), or start is restore without an uploaded backup ("Choose the backup file first.").

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up in this core (no setup network manager or setup flow). The error is the phone's generic sentence (setup_flow.said).

get.summary: Wi-Fi networks in range, without the setup network
get.description: A Wi-Fi scan read while the setup network is hosted (Finding 099: the phone stays connected), for the Network step. The setup network itself (gexis-setup) is left out. The connected network comes first, then saved ones, then the rest by signal; a hidden network is not listed. Answers only while setup is running.

200.description: The networks in range (empty if the scan failed).

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up in this core (no setup network manager or setup flow). The error is the phone's generic sentence (setup_flow.said).

get.summary: Each audio output and whether it has its own volume control
get.description: For the Volume choice under the Output step: each output by its name as Settings lists it, and whether it has a hardware volume control of its own. Without one, Hardware volume cannot be chosen, as in Settings (ADR-0127 §2). Answers only while setup is running.

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up in this core (no setup network manager or setup flow). The error is the phone's generic sentence (setup_flow.said).

get.summary: The plugins the release ships, as setup offers them
get.description: Every plugin the release ships beyond the built-in sources and uploaded plugins (ADR-0128 decision 1): what it is, where it downloads from, and the notice it must show first (ADR-0098). Answers only while setup is running.

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up in this core (no setup network manager or setup flow). The error is the phone's generic sentence (setup_flow.said).

get.summary: The Screen step: what is connected and every known model
get.description: The Screen step of setup (ADR-0109): what the connected screen reports, the tested model that suggests (or null), every model gexis knows, and which choices would change nothing about the picture now shown (those do not restart the player or ask Keep this screen?). The current rotation setting is used for that comparison. Answers only while setup is running.

409.description: Setup is not running: the setup network is not open, failed or joining, and the device does not need setup (ADR-0104). Error: "Setup has already finished. Open the player at its address instead."

503.description: Setup is not wired up, or screen detection is not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Whether setup is needed and the setup network's state
get.description: Answers ADR-0104 §5's inputs: whether this device needs setup and the state of the setup network (gexis-setup). The setup network's password is only ever included for a loopback caller (the panel, ADR-0035 §6); to any caller over the network it is always null. Without a setup network manager the answer is {"needed": false, "network": "unmanaged"}. Every /setup/ request from a phone also marks the setup page as in use.

200.description: The setup status (the password null unless the caller is the panel on loopback).

get.summary: List the visualiser skins installed on the device
get.description: Every skin in the installed skin pack, with what it shows and whether the `skin_corpus` setting includes it (ADR-0050). What a skin shows is read from its own declarations, not from where it lives (ADR-0019 as amended): a meter, a spectrum, both, a turntable or a tape. The list is read again only when the pack changes. Used by the skin picker.

200.description: The skins and the corpus currently chosen.

503.description: Skins are not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Get a skin's preview picture
get.description: Serves the skin's own picture - its `screen.bgr`, or for a skin without one its meter background (`bgr.filename`) - and nothing generated (ADR-0050). The name never reaches the filesystem: it is matched against the parsed skins, and the file served is the one that skin declares beside its own `meters.txt`. With `w` of 480 or 960 a scaled JPEG copy is served, cached for a day (ADR-0050 as amended 2026-10-03); any other width, or a scaling failure, serves the original.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The skin's name exactly as `/skins` lists it, URL-encoded; may contain slashes.

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: Width in pixels of a scaled copy. Only 480 and 960 are made; any other value serves the original picture.

200.description: The picture: the skin's own file (PNG or JPEG), or a scaled JPEG sent with `Cache-Control: max-age=86400`.

404.description: No skin of that name (`no such skin`), or the skin declares no picture that exists (`that skin has no picture`).

503.description: Skins are not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Live playback state over a WebSocket
get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket that pushes the whole playback state as one JSON text message (schema `State`). The current snapshot is sent once on connect, then a fresh full snapshot each time the state store changes - pushed, never on a fixed tick (ADR-0018). The socket is publish-only (ADR-0028): anything a client sends is read and ignored, and commands go through the POST routes instead. There is no ping from the server on this socket.

101.description: Switching Protocols. Each message the server then sends is a text frame holding a `State` JSON object.

400.description: The request was not a WebSocket upgrade. aiohttp answers this itself, as plain text rather than the JSON error object.

get.summary: Read the Music folder's free and total space
get.description: The Music folder's free and total space, for setup's *Where is your music?* step, and whether the Music share is closed to new files because the card is nearly full (ADR-0115 decision 27, cited with the Music folder row). Read only.

get.summary: Say whether the caller is the panel or a remote device
get.description: Answers whether the request came from the panel or from another device. The panel always arrives on loopback (127.0.0.1 or ::1) and anything else is a phone or a computer on the LAN (ADR-0035 §6). The web UI asks once so the same page knows which surface it is drawing.

post.summary: Report that somebody touched the panel
post.description: The panel tells the core it was touched, since touches land in whichever window holds the screen and the core cannot see them. It counts as attention for the visualiser's timers and wakes a screen in standby (ADR-0135). Accepted from loopback only: a phone's request would wake a screen in standby and count as attention nobody paid. No body is read.

403.description: The request did not come from the panel (not loopback): `only the panel reports touches`.

get.summary: Open the touchpad relay WebSocket
get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket that lets a phone act as the panel's touchpad and keyboard (ADR-0121). A connection from loopback is the panel; any other is a phone (ADR-0035 §6). A phone may send move, tap, text, key, scroll and zoom messages, which the core relays unchanged to every connected panel; the panel may send over and focus, relayed to every connected phone. Anything else, any non-text frame and any frame over 2048 bytes is dropped, and while the Phone touchpad setting (`phone_touchpad`) is off every relayed message is dropped too. A `{"t":"ping"}` from either side is always answered to the sender alone with `{"t":"pong"}`; when a phone disconnects, every panel is sent `{"t":"gone","phones":<n>}`. The socket is separate from `/state`, which stays publish-only (ADR-0028); the server sends a WebSocket heartbeat every 20 seconds.

101.description: Switching protocols. Text frames are JSON objects with a `t` field: from a phone, one of PanelTouchpadFromPhone; from the panel, one of PanelTouchpadFromPanel; to either, PanelTouchpadPong; to a panel, also PanelTouchpadGone. Relayed messages arrive exactly as the other side sent them.

schema.description: Any message that can travel on the touchpad socket, in either direction.

post.summary: Send a transport command to the active renderer
post.description: Sends play, pause, next, previous, shuffle or repeat to whichever renderer holds the device - never to a renderer by name, since a command to one that is not active would be an acquisition (ADR-0037 §1). The command must be declared by the active renderer and listed in the state's `controls.available` right now (ADR-0037 §2). `shuffle` and `repeat` take a JSON body; the others take none. A 200 means the command was sent; its effect arrives on /state.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The transport command (`TRANSPORT_COMMANDS` in adapters/base.py).

requestBody.description: Only for `shuffle` (`{"on": true|false}`) and `repeat` (`{"mode": "off"|"all"|"one"}`); ignored for the other commands.

200.description: The command was sent to the active renderer.

400.description: `shuffle` without a boolean `on`, or `repeat` without `mode` set to off, all or one.

404.description: The command is not one of the transport commands.

409.description: Nothing is active, the active renderer does not declare the command, or the command cannot work on it right now (not in `controls.available`) (a source with no capabilities declared declares none).

502.description: The active renderer did not take the command (its API refused, was unreachable, or it implements no such method).

503.description: Transport is not wired up in this core.

post.summary: Set the volume as a slider percentage
post.description: Sets the volume to a position of the panel's slider, 0-100 (ADR-0028's command surface). With a renderer playing, the panel acts as a remote: the position goes to that renderer's own volume control and reaches the DAC the way its own changes do (ADR-0053); with nothing to be a remote for, it is written to the hardware mixer over the slider's -45..0 dB range (ADR-0034). The resulting level arrives on /state under `volume`.

200.description: The level was sent. `percent` echoes the request, as a number.

400.description: The body is not JSON, has no `percent`, `percent` is not a number, or it is outside 0-100.

503.description: Volume control is not wired up in this core.

post.summary: Mute or unmute the output
post.description: Mutes or unmutes the output (ADR-0028's command surface). The new state is published on /state as `volume.muted`. It fails with 409 while the volume level has not been read yet, a real window just after start.

400.description: The body is not JSON or `muted` is missing or not a boolean.

409.description: The mute could not be set: the volume level is not known yet.

503.description: Mute is not wired up in this core.

get.summary: Whether the Home Assistant dashboard is up, and whether it can be shown
get.description: The dashboard set in `dashboard_url` (ADR-0156), checked as the idle page is: unconfigured, unreachable within 5 seconds, an HTTP error status, or headers that forbid framing make it not embeddable, and `message` says what to set and where - in Home Assistant, framing is *Send X-Frame-Options* off (Settings → System → Network; `use_x_frame_options: false` under `http` before 2026.10, Finding 132). The player changes nothing in Home Assistant. Asked by the panel each time it puts the dashboard up. Headers only: whether Home Assistant lets the player in without a login is not checked.

200.description: Up or not, who asked, and whether the address can be shown.

example.message: Home Assistant does not allow its pages to be shown inside another page. In Home Assistant, turn off Send X-Frame-Options (Settings → System → Network → HTTP server → More options), or set use_x_frame_options: false under http before version 2026.10.

503.description: The dashboard is not wired up in this core.

post.summary: Put the Home Assistant dashboard up or take it down
post.description: From the panel's button and edge tab, a phone, or Home Assistant itself - a `rest_command` or automation (ADR-0156). Music is not touched; the dashboard stays until it is taken down. A person's `show` counts as attention, so the visualiser goes down. `?by=schedule` is the panel putting it up in place of the idle screen during the dashboard's times; the schedule takes down only what it put up, and a person's `show` over it makes it theirs.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: `show` puts the dashboard up; `hide` takes it down.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: `schedule` when the panel puts it up in place of the idle screen; left out for anyone else.

200.description: Done; whether the dashboard is now up.

404.description: `action` is neither `show` nor `hide`: `unknown action <action>`.

503.description: The dashboard is not wired up in this core.

post.summary: A real tap, text or key on the panel
post.description: The panel asks for this when the phone's touchpad pointer is over a page from another site in a frame - the Home Assistant dashboard - which the panel's own made-up events cannot reach (ADR-0157). A tap becomes a touch from a virtual touchscreen at that fraction of the screen; text and the keys Backspace, Enter and Tab become key presses from a virtual keyboard, each character the key (with Shift or AltGr) that makes it on the panel's keyboard layout. Only the panel's own session receives them.

200.description: Made; for text, `done` is false when a character is not on the panel's keyboard layout (it is left out, the rest typed).

400.description: Not a tap, text or key, or out of range: x and y outside 0-1, text empty or over 500 characters, a key other than Backspace, Enter or Tab.

503.description: Panel input is not wired up in this core, or the virtual devices could not be made.
