examples: Help others with this DAC: share how it works

ReportsScreenResult.description: Each tap's distance from its circle, and whether all four landed within 6 % of the screen's diagonal.

ReportsScreenShow.description: Show (`true`) or take down (anything else) the test pattern on the panel.

ReportsScreenShown.description: The pattern is up: this check's number and whether the screen has touch. It goes away by itself after 120 s.

ReportsScreenTaps.description: The panel's four corner taps, in the screen's own pixels.

ReportsStatus.description: The problem report being prepared (ADR-0138 §1): its state and checklist, and once ready the file's name, size, contents and what was taken out. A ready report is kept an hour; after that, and before any, only `state: idle`.

ReportsTones.description: One line per tone (44.1, 96 and 192 kHz): played, and the rate and format the card ran at.

examples: 44.1 kHz: played, the card at 44.1 kHz S32_LE

SettingsActionRun.description: An action started. Answered at once: the action itself may still be running.

SettingsComponent.description: A plugin's downloaded software, as its switch and its Retry and Remove rows carry it (ADR-0100): where it comes from and how far a download has got.

updated.description: Unix time of the last change.

SettingsCondition.description: A row's `onlyWhen` (ADR-0044 §3): one `[key, value]` pair, or a list of pairs that must all hold. The value is a literal the key must hold, the string `*any*` (holds anything non-empty), `{"not": value}` (shown unless the key holds that value) or `{"in": [values]}` (shown while the key holds one of them). The core has already worked the answer out into the row's `visible`; this is for clients that want the rule.

oneOf.description: Several pairs, all of which must hold.

SettingsDevice.description: The Settings header (ADR-0048 §5): the stored name, and the system's own hostname and address - which disagree after a rename until the restart.

SettingsDocument.description: A page the panel draws as a document (ADR-0099, ADR-0116): a title, then sections of paragraphs with, for Legal and Credits, the components' entries and, for the change logs, each release's notes.

url.description: Change logs: where every release's notes are.

SettingsGroup.description: A Settings category - Audio, Sources, Library, Handoff, Display, Enrichment, Plugins, System - with its rows and sub-headings in order.

SettingsHeading.description: A sub-heading inside a group (`type: "group"`): it has no key and no value. Its `onlyWhen` governs the rows under it, already folded into their `visible`.

indicatorOf.description: The switch whose service this heading reports on.

SettingsIndicator.description: A switched-on service's connection, said on the heading above its rows (ADR-0129): the core's own reading, as a tone and a word or two.

SettingsInterval.description: One time span of an `intervals` row (ADR-0135, the standby times): from a start to an end time on the days it starts; it may run past midnight. Start and end may not be equal.

SettingsItemActed.description: The outcome of an item action. A refusal the sheet can show - a wrong password, a server that did not answer, a restore that failed - comes back with status 200, `ok: false` and the sentence in `error`. Browse and folders answer the items found.

notice.description: Wi-Fi join while a cable is plugged in: the cable stays in use (ADR-0123).

login.description: Shares: the server needs a user and password.

crumbs.description: Browse and folders: the path back up, a step each.

SettingsItemAction.description: What to do with one item of a list row. `action` defaults to `join`. Which actions a list takes: `wifi` join, forget; `bt_trusted` forget; `restore` join (restore it, then the device reboots), forget (delete the file); `lyrion-server.shares` browse, folders, add, forget; `lyrion-server.usb_folders` browse, add, forget.

name.description: The item: a network's name, a device's name, a backup's file name, a server's name, a share's address or a USB drive (browse, add) or folder address (forget).

password.description: Wi-Fi join; a share's browse, folders, add.

server.description: Shares browse: the server found by the search.

folder.description: USB folders browse, add: the folder on the drive.

SettingsItems.description: A list row's items. `error` is there only when the list's source is missing (Wi-Fi without NetworkManager).

SettingsListItem.description: One item of a `list` row (ADR-0044 §1): a Wi-Fi network, a paired Bluetooth device, a Lyrion server, a backup, a music share or a USB folder. `name`, `meta`, `bars` and `state` are always there; the rest depend on the list.

name.description: What the item is called on screen, and what an item action sends back as `name` (a network's name, a backup's file name, a server's name).

bars.description: Signal strength as four bars, for a Wi-Fi network; null elsewhere.

state.description: `connected`/`saved`/`open`/`locked` for Wi-Fi; `connected`/`saved` for Bluetooth; `current`/`found` for Lyrion servers; `saved` for a backup or a share added; `found` for something that can be added.

secured.description: Wi-Fi: the network needs a password.

details.description: Wi-Fi, the connected network only: label and value pairs (Signal, Speed, Band, Address).

address.description: A Lyrion server's address (what `lms_server` stores), a Bluetooth device's address, a share's address, or a USB folder's drive/folder.

path.description: Bluetooth: the device's BlueZ object path.

broken.description: Backup: the file cannot be restored (empty or damaged); listed so it can be forgotten.

server.description: Shares search: the server to browse.

share.description: Shares: the item is a share or a folder in one.

folder.description: USB folders: the folder on the drive.

pending.description: USB folders: a drive plugged in with no folder chosen.

login.description: Shares: the share needs its password again.

user.description: Shares: the user name stored for it.

SettingsMusicSpace.description: The Music folder's file system: free and total bytes and the same as text, null when they cannot be read; and whether the Music share is closed to new files because the card is nearly full (ADR-0115 decision 27).

SettingsPage.description: Every setting, grouped as the Settings screen shows them, and the header's facts.

SettingsRow.description: One setting as `/settings` publishes it (ADR-0035, ADR-0044 §6): every registry field except `default`, with what the core works out added. The panel draws only rows with `visible: true`; a client that wants the whole inventory (ADR-0022) has it. Fields beyond the ones always present depend on the row's type and are present only when they apply.

key.description: The setting's key; a plugin's rows are prefixed with its id (ADR-0086).

type.description: `toggle`, `choice`, `number`, `text`, `multi` and `intervals` take a value through PUT; `action` is run through POST; `list` has items; `readonly` and `document` (a page served at `/notices/{name}`) take nothing.

marks.description: ADR-0022's inventory mark: R recorded, H hardcoded, N new, ? a decision still owed.

value.description: What is in force: a stored value, the flash-time seed, a system default or the registry's default. Boolean for a toggle, number for a number, string for a choice or text, a list of strings for a multi, a list of SettingsInterval for intervals; for a list, the stored server address (`lms_server`), the connected network (`wifi`) or null; for a readonly row, its text or null; null for an action or document.

wired.description: Something acts on the row; an unwired row refuses writes with 409.

visible.description: Whether the panel shows it now: its `onlyWhen`, its heading's and its group's, and the hardware.

options.description: A choice's or multi's options; for `optionsFrom` rows, what the source offers now.

optionsFrom.description: The source the options are drawn from (ADR-0044 §4).

optionLabels.description: What each option is called on screen, where the value is a key.

optionTags.description: A word beside an option, e.g. *Tested*.

optionProblems.description: A line under an option owners reported a problem with.

unavailable.description: Options the hardware cannot honour now, each with why (ADR-0055); writing one is refused with 409.

max.description: A number's upper bound, or how many spans an intervals row takes.

secret.description: A key, token or password; left out of problem reports.

pattern.description: A text value's form, matched whole; empty always passes.

invalid.description: The sentence a value not matching `pattern` is refused with.

warn.description: A warning shown before the change: about the row, or per option of a choice (ADR-0044 §2).

hold.description: The action is confirmed by holding.

restart.description: true: changing the value restarts the device. "core": it restarts the player's core instead (lms_server), the device staying up.

surfaced.description: False: kept in the API, not drawn as a row of its own.

kind.description: What a list or action is about, e.g. `server` (a list whose chosen item is stored), `network`, `device`, `backup`, `cable`, `report`, `hardware`.

empty.description: A list's line when it has no items.

discover.description: A list whose items are fetched from `/settings/{key}/items` when its sheet opens.

manual.description: A server list's line for entering an address by hand.

document.description: A document row's page name for `/notices/{name}`.

items.description: A list's items, sent with the row for the lists that read them cheaply (paired Bluetooth devices, backups, shares, USB folders).

progress.description: The library row: how far a scan has got.

busy.description: The library row: Lyrion is working without a measure.

uploaded.description: A plugin uploaded by the user (ADR-0106).

SettingsRowStatus.description: What a plugin last said about its own row (ADR-0119): `done` with a few words, or `failed` with a sentence. Kept in memory only.

SettingsWrite.description: A new value for one setting. Its type follows the row: boolean (toggle), one of `options` (choice), a list of options (multi, never empty), a number within `min`..`max` (number), text of at most 500 characters (text; empty clears it back to the default), a list of SettingsInterval (intervals), or an address (a `server` list).

SettingsWritten.description: The value as stored - checked and normalised, e.g. text trimmed, a multi in the registry's order - and the settings revision this save made.

revision.description: The settings revision after the save; the same revision is broadcast on the live state.

SetupAnswers.description: The answers setup has saved so far, which a page resumes from (ADR-0104 §4). Only the keys answered are present, plus has_password. The Wi-Fi password itself is never returned.

has_password.description: A Wi-Fi password has been saved.

timezone.description: The time zone; also sets the Wi-Fi country.

output.description: The output, as GET /setup/outputs names it (output_device).

lms_mode.description: Lyrion: find a server once on the network, use the typed address, or none.

lms.description: The typed Lyrion server address, used only with lms_mode address.

screen.description: The screen model's label as Settings stores it (Maker/Model, ADR-0109).

second_player.description: On a restore under another name: false means it is the same player, keeping the backup's identities (ADR-0131).

plugins.description: The ids of the offered plugins chosen (ADR-0128), sorted.

start.description: A new player or a restore from a backup (ADR-0131 §1).

step.description: The page's step to resume at; set to wifi after a failed join.

error.description: The last join's failure; the password was dropped (ADR-0031 amendment 5).

SetupAnswersChange.description: Answers to save; every key optional, unknown keys refused. The same keys as SetupAnswers, plus password, without has_password, backup or error.

password.description: The Wi-Fi password; stored until the join succeeds or fails, never returned.

screen.description: A known model's label; not together with headless true.

SetupBackupReview.description: What an uploaded backup would bring (ADR-0131 §3-4), without anything put back yet.

name.description: The name of the player it was made on.

made.description: When it was made, seconds since the epoch.

identities.description: What a second player would leave behind, of what this backup holds.

newer.description: A newer version of gexis made it.

settings.description: Its settings as setup applies them, by key.

enabled.description: The plugin ids it stores switched on.

brings.description: What it carries besides settings, a line each (paired Bluetooth devices, sign-ins, playlists and so on).

sections.description: Everything it brings by Settings section, for the review; empty if it could not be grouped.

file.description: The uploaded file's name as given in ?name= (up to 120 characters).

SetupFinished.description: What setup's last panel screen says: the network joined, what became of Lyrion, and whether and why the player restarts.

ssid.description: The Wi-Fi joined; null on the cable.

restart_for.description: Why it restarts: a new name (ADR-0048), a new screen (ADR-0109), both, or a restored backup (ADR-0131).

SetupFinishing.description: Setup's apply has started (or was already running).

keep_question.description: The restart will ask Keep this screen? on the panel (ADR-0109 as amended 2026-10-02), which the phone says before the owner leaves.

SetupLibrary.description: What became of the Lyrion server choice once on the home network.

state.description: off: the Lyrion client switched off; given: the typed address kept; found: exactly one server found and used; several: more than one found, left to Settings; none: none found; unchanged: nothing chosen or a restore.

address.description: The server's address, for given and found.

name.description: The found server's name (host name, else its library name, else its address), for found.

SetupNetwork.description: A Wi-Fi network in range, as the settings sheet draws it.

meta.description: The line under it: Connected (with speed), Saved, Secured or Open.

details.description: For the connected network: label and value pairs (Signal, Speed, Band, Address).

SetupOutput.description: An audio output for the Output step's volume choice.

option.description: Its name as Settings lists it; an unplugged one ends " — nothing connected".

hardware.description: It has a volume control of its own, so Hardware volume can be chosen (ADR-0127 §2).

SetupPlugin.description: A plugin the release ships, as setup offers it (ADR-0128).

summary.description: What it is, or where it downloads from.

notice.description: The notice it must show first (ADR-0098).

component.description: The download it waits for on the settling screen, or null if it downloads nothing.

label.description: Maker/Model, as stored in the screen setting.

tested.description: Tested by the project or reported working by owners.

problem.description: A problem owners reported, as a line.

skins.description: The visualiser skin pack it gets, as WIDTHxHEIGHT (ADR-0111), or null.

skin_count.description: How many skins that pack holds.

SetupScreenChoices.description: The Screen step's page (ADR-0109). A suggestion means the screen was recognised; a screen connected without one is uncertain; nothing connected is none.

connector.description: The port: HDMI-A-1, HDMI-A-2, or DSI-1 for a DSI panel (ADR-0158), which has no EDID.

panel.description: A DSI panel's I2C drivers, by which it is recognised (ADR-0158); empty on HDMI.

suggested.description: The tested model the report suggests.

unchanged.description: Ids of the models whose picture is the one shown now: choosing them changes nothing.

SetupStatus.description: Whether setup is needed and the setup network's state (ADR-0104 §5). The setup network's password is never included for a caller over the network: password is null except for a loopback caller (the panel), and the /state broadcast never carries it. When no setup network manager runs, only needed (false) and network ("unmanaged") are present.

needed.description: This device has not been set up yet.

network.description: The setup network's state: open while it is hosted, joining while the device joins a network, failed when it could not start, done on setup's last panel screen, online on the home network.

ssid.description: The setup network's name while open (always gexis-setup), else null.

password.description: The setup network's password: only to a loopback caller (the panel) and only while open. Always null to anyone else.

address.description: Where the setup page is: on the setup network while open, or the device's LAN address when a new device on Ethernet is set up over it.

reason.description: Why the setup network failed to start, or why the last join failed, in a sentence.

failed.description: The network the last join failed on.

target.description: The network being joined, while joining.

phones.description: Phones associated with the setup network while open, else 0.

finished.description: Setup's last panel screen, while network is done.

page_opened.description: A phone has opened the setup page while the network is open.

channel.description: The Wi-Fi channel the setup network is on while open.

rotate_at.description: When the setup network moves to its next channel if nobody joins, as wall-clock seconds since the epoch; null when not scheduled.

State.description: The whole playback state, as pushed on the /state WebSocket (model.py `PlaybackState.to_json`). Every message is a full snapshot, never a diff, so a client needs to keep nothing between messages.

active.description: The renderer id holding the device, or null when nobody does (a routine state, ADR-0027).

available.description: Renderer id to whether its backend is reachable, independent of `active`. Has an entry for every known renderer.

metadata.description: The active renderer's track; all fields null when nobody is active.

capabilities.description: Renderer id to its declared contract (ADR-0013). Static for the process.

handoff.description: A takeover in flight, or null.

volume.description: The hardware mixer's level, or null before it has been read once.

fixed_output.description: True when the device does not attenuate at all (ADR-0046); the volume slider does not apply.

meters.description: Whether the visualiser can have levels on this output (ADR-0055 §6).

sources.description: One entry per installed source (ADR-0086). Static for the process.

settings_revision.description: Bumped on every settings write (ADR-0035); refetch GET /settings when it changes.

pictures_revision.description: Bumped when the library's pictures change (ADR-0059's sweep finishing); drop cached artist photos when it changes.

controls.description: What the active renderer can do right now (ADR-0037 §2), or null when nobody is active.

queue.description: The active renderer's queue (Lyrion only, ADR-0038), or null.

pairing.description: A Bluetooth pairing request waiting for an answer (ADR-0045), or null.

components.description: Downloads a plugin makes when switched on, by component name: phase, bytes of total, attempt, error (ADR-0100 as amended).

setup.description: First-boot setup and the setup network's public status (ADR-0104); never carries the password (always null there). Null until decided.

update.description: The installed release and what the updater is doing: state, steps, download share, and `active` while an install runs (ADR-0110).

screen_confirm.description: The panel's *Keep this screen?* question: model in use, the one it reverts to, and when the countdown ends in epoch seconds (ADR-0109).

screen_new.description: A different screen attached at start, waiting for an answer (ADR-0109 as amended 2026-10-03).

screen_check.description: The hardware report's screen check: the test pattern and what the corner taps measured (ADR-0126).

settling.description: The first start after setup, until its chosen downloads finish: `phase` and each item's state (ADR-0128).

personalise.description: `pending` while first use's part 2 is owed (ADR-0149), else null.

resetting.description: True once a factory reset is confirmed and the device is restarting into it (ADR-0132).

name.description: The skin's name, as its section in the pack's meters.txt gives it.

in_corpus.description: Whether the chosen `skin_corpus` includes this skin, as the visualiser chooses: by its kind, or for Fanart by whether it has an artist-photo frame.

preview.description: The URL of its preview picture (`/skins/{name}/preview`, name URL-encoded).

VisualiserSkins.description: The skins installed on the device and the corpus the `skin_corpus` setting chooses.

skins.description: Every installed skin; empty when no pack is installed.

corpus.description: The `skin_corpus` setting's value as stored (`All` when unset). An unrecognised value is treated as `All` for `in_corpus`; `Random` is the old name for `All`.

by.description: Who put it up: `asked` (a person, the panel, a phone or Home Assistant) or `schedule`; null when it is down.

PanelDashboardCheck.description: The dashboard's state and the check of its address (ADR-0156).

by.description: `asked`, `schedule`, or null when it is down.

url.description: The dashboard's address, or null when none is set.

embeddable.description: Whether the address answered and allows being shown in a frame.

reason.description: Why not: `unconfigured`, `unreachable`, `http <status>` or `refuses framing`; null when it can be shown.

message.description: The sentence the panel shows for `reason`, saying what to set and where; null when it can be shown.

PanelInput.description: One real input on the panel (ADR-0157).

x.description: For a tap: the fraction of the screen's width.

y.description: For a tap: the fraction of the screen's height.
